verdict.rationale: Honeybadger documents some of its own noise controls: it groups identical errors so they are not reported separately, users can customize grouping with fingerprints, and users can choose which error events trigger a notification. These loosely approximate mute rules, but the evidence never shows spike protection, per-key rate limits, or explicit mute/ignore rules. Missing for 10: spike protection, per-key rate limiting, explicit mute/ignore/snooze rules, notification throttling during a bad deploy, and independent corroboration of alert-noise reduction.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can fight alert fatigue with spike protection, per-key rate limits, and mute/ignore rules so one bad deploy doesn't page the whole team all night

citations.quote: You get to choose which error events result in a notification or ticket being created
You can customize the grouping for each exception by changing the error class name, component, or stack trace—or by sending a custom fingerprint.
